messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in New York with reading room and fiction section, in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and children's section, and in Chicago with cafe and reading room. We need to use the function public_library_find_nearby. We need to call it three times with appropriate parameters.

We need to provide the function calls. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby({location: string, facilities: ...}). The facilities parameter can be one of the listed options: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the facilities parameter seems to accept a single value? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." The type is union of those strings or array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] indicates array of "Cafe"? The type is ambiguous. But likely we need to pass an array of facilities? The description: "Facilities and sections in public library." So maybe we pass an array of strings like ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]. But the type says "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That suggests that facilities can be a string or an array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. But maybe they want to pass an array of strings. Let's assume we pass an array of strings.

Thus for New York: location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

For Los Angeles: location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

For Chicago: location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to call the function three times. We'll produce separate calls.
